land.text: French Cameroun, independent on 1 January 1960 as the Republic of Cameroon

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's French Fifth Republic shape for 1958-1959 holds the French trust territory (1,771 of the 1,973 cells of modern Cameroon); the 1960 French shape holds 15. No Cliopatria row exists for French Cameroons.

land.text: British Southern Cameroons, which became West Cameroon on 1 October 1961

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's British Gold Coast shape for 1960 (954,027 km2) holds 185 of the 191 cells of the Northwest and Southwest regions; the pages name the owner as the United Kingdom's trust territory of British Cameroons, which the British administered with Nigeria. The Nigeria dossier uses the same counterpart for Northern Cameroons.

capitals.name: Yaoundé
capitals.note: Cameroon page infobox 'Capital: Yaoundé'; the page names only one capital. Coordinates are Natural Earth's.

keyframe_review.note: 424,323 km2 for 1960: French Cameroun without British Southern Cameroons. The page gives only the modern area (475,442 km2); the 1960 shape is 0.89 of it and the 1961 shape differs from it by exactly the Northwest and Southwest regions (182 of its 186 added cells lie in them), as the 1 October 1961 union (British Cameroons page) predicts. Independence on 1 January 1960 (infobox 'Independence of French Cameroons from France: 1 January 1960').

minus.text: Bakassi, the peninsula of 665 km2 on the Gulf of Guinea held by Nigeria until the handovers of 2006 and 2008; the page gives only a box, 4 deg 25 min-5 deg 10 min N and 8 deg 20 min-9 deg 8 min E; the centre and the 25 km radius are the researcher's

correction.text: Republic of Cameroon within its 1961 frontier but without the Bakassi peninsula, valid 1961-2007; the shape's years change from 1961-2023 to 1961-2007

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 465,691 km2 against the infobox 475,442 km2 is a ratio of 0.98, so the area is fine; but the shape follows the modern frontier and so holds Bakassi (2 of its 4 cells) from 1961. The Bakassi page says the peninsula 'remained under Calabar administration in Nigeria until ICJ judgement of 2002' and was handed over on 14 August 2006 (north) and 14 August 2008 (final parts). Remove Bakassi for 1961-2007; the 2008 keyframe restores it. The Southern Cameroons (Northwest and Southwest regions) are right from 1 October 1961 (British Cameroons page); the shape's years 1961-2023 are to be read as 1961-2007 for this corrected shape.

correction.text: The 1961-2023 Cliopatria outline of the Republic of Cameroon, Bakassi included, unchanged: only the years change (2008-2023)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from 14 August 2008 'handed the final parts of Bakassi over to Cameroon', so the whole 1961 outline of Cliopatria, Bakassi included, holds for 2008-2023. The northern part had come on 14 August 2006 ('a ceremony on 14 August marked the formal handover of the northern part of the peninsula'); at 665 km2 for the whole peninsula, that half is about one grid cell, so it is carried by the ledger caption only.
Same outline as the 1961-2023 shape (465,691 km2); no page opened records a change in 2024.

region.text: French Cameroun, the former French mandate and trust territory

ledger.note: 1 January 1960: French Cameroun becomes independent as the Republic of Cameroon. 'On 1 January 1960, French Cameroun gained independence from France under President Ahmadou Ahidjo as the Republic of Cameroon.' (infobox 'Independence of French Cameroons from France: 1 January 1960').

1 October 1961: British Southern Cameroons joins the Republic of Cameroon. 'Southern Cameroons became West Cameroon, a constituent state of the Federal Republic of Cameroon, later that year on 1 October 1961', after the UN-administered plebiscite of 11 February 1961 in which 'the Southern Area voted to join Cameroon' while the Muslim-majority Northern Area opted for Nigeria (Northern Cameroons became the Sardauna Province of Northern Nigeria on 1 June 1961). Cameroon page: 'the British Southern Cameroons gained independence ... and merged into the Republic of Cameroon'. The page names Southern Cameroons, not its provinces; the Northwest and Southwest regions are the researcher's reading, confirmed by the Cliopatria shapes (the 1961 shape adds exactly those regions to the 1960 shape).

1 October 1961: the Federal Republic of Cameroon. 'merged into the Republic of Cameroon to form the Federal Republic of Cameroon'; infobox 'establishment of the Federal Republic of Cameroon: 1 October 1961'. Same state, land and colour.

20 May 1972: the federation is abolished and the country becomes the United Republic of Cameroon. Infobox 'Cameroonian constitutional referendum of 1972 and establishment of the Unitary State: 20 May 1972'; text 'The country was renamed the United Republic of Cameroon in 1972' and 'The federation was abandoned in 1972'. West Cameroon ceases to be a state of a federation but the land is unchanged.
1984: back to the Republic of Cameroon. 'In 1984, President Paul Biya restored the name Republic of Cameroon via presidential decree.' The page gives no month.

region.text: the northern part of the Bakassi peninsula

ledger.note: 14 August 2006: Nigeria hands over the northern part of Bakassi. 'a ceremony on 14 August marked the formal handover of the northern part of the peninsula'; the Greentree Agreement of 13 June 2006 ('President Olusegun Obasanjo of Nigeria and President Paul Biya of Cameroon resolved the dispute') followed the ICJ judgment of 10 October 2002, which found 'sovereignty over Bakassi did indeed rest with Cameroon' on the basis of the Anglo-German agreements. The Cameroon page agrees: 'The northern portion of the territory was formally handed over to the Cameroonian government in August 2006.' The remainder 'stayed under Nigerian civil authority for two more years'.

region.text: the final parts of the Bakassi peninsula

ledger.note: 14 August 2008: the rest of Bakassi passes to Cameroon. Nigeria 'handed the final parts of Bakassi over to Cameroon on 14 August 2008 as planned'. The peninsula (665 km2) had 'remained under Calabar administration in Nigeria until ICJ judgement of 2002'; the Cliopatria shape already holds it, the 2008 keyframe restores it.

wars.name: Bakassi dispute with Nigeria

zones.text: the Bakassi peninsula, 665 km2, between the Cross River and Rio del Rey estuaries

wars.outcome: Cameroon won at law: the ICJ judgment of 10 October 2002 gave it sovereignty; the Greentree Agreement (13 June 2006) led to the handover of the northern part on 14 August 2006 and of the final parts on 14 August 2008.
wars.note: 'In 1981 the two countries went to the brink of war over Bakassi'; 'More armed clashes broke out in the early 1990s'; Cameroon took the case to the ICJ on 29 March 1994. The pages date no campaign that took or held ground, so no contest_start is recorded; Bakassi is drawn as Nigerian-held until the gains of 2006 and 2008. The Cameroon page also notes a dispute over an area around Lake Chad in 1981 (Bakassi page) without detail.

wars.name: Anglophone Crisis
wars.outcome: Ongoing: 'separatists started a guerilla war for the independence of the Anglophone region as the Federal Republic of Ambazonia' and 'the insurgency spread across the Northwest and Southwest regions'.
wars.note: The page gives no territory held by the separatists, so the war moves no border and no zone or rebel dossier is recorded; the year of the start (2017) is the page's surrounding text, the declaration of Ambazonia is undated on the page (it only says 1 October is regarded by Ambazonians as their independence day). The 'to' year is the dataset horizon, not an end.

certainty.note: Colonial and treaty frontiers. The exception is Bakassi, 'never permanently delineated' until the 2002 judgment and the 2006-2008 handovers (soft there before 2008). The page also mentions a 1981 dispute over an area around Lake Chad without details.

notes: Page budget 3 of 2 (Cameroon, British Cameroons, Bakassi): the third page was needed because the only post-1961 border event, Bakassi, is undated on the Cameroon page. (1) Cliopatria's 1961-2023 shape includes Bakassi and so is adjusted (see keyframes); because the grid cells are about 250 km2 and Bakassi is 665 km2, Bakassi is 2-3 cells wide and the effect is small. Bakassi is not in the gazetteer: the radius {lon 8.55, lat 4.65, 25 km} is the researcher's; a gazetteer place 'Bakassi' should replace it (listed for the gazetteer agent). (2) The counterpart of the 1961 gain is 'british-gold-coast', because Cliopatria's British Gold Coast 1960 shape is what holds the Northwest and Southwest regions (as the Nigeria dossier does for Northern Cameroons); the pages name the owner as British Cameroons (a UN trust territory), for which no Cliopatria row or dossier exists. (3) The Anglophone Crisis (since 2017) is recorded as a war without zones because no page opened says the separatists held ground; 'Ambazonia' is not given a rebel dossier. (4) The 1960 shape's infobox check is indirect: the pages give no area for French Cameroons; the two-part British Cameroons infobox area is 89,526 km2, of which the Southern share is not given. (5) The 1960 handover from France is carried by the French Fifth Republic's 1958-1959 shape; its dossier should lose Cameroon at 1960.
